A few preparations are necessary before your service engineer can set up your machine. The following
preparations must be carried out by a professionally qualified person.
Description
OK
Issue
Flat and clean surface
Clean environment
Space above min. 250 mm (11.8 in)
Stable table capable of bearing up to:
• 70 kg (Cameo, Légacy, E'2c, Shotmaster c)
• 110 kg (E'2, E'4, Shotmaster s, Shotmaster ms)
• 140 kg (E'4 x-wide)
• 170 kg (E'6, Shotmaster s-pro, Shotmaster ms-pro)
Table height 800 mm (31.5 in)
Countertop cutout, download here: https://bit.ly/3xT5TTM
Separate electrical lines for each machine
Electrical mains protected by RCD or RCCB
Water mains shutoff valve with a non-return valve (type EA or accord-
ing to local regulation)
Descaling cartridge or carbon filter as minimum
Water pressure 2.5 - 4 bars (32.3 - 58 psi) (250 - 400 KPa)
Pressure reducer (only if pressure is above 4 bars)
Flow rate above 200 L/h (Enigma, Shotmaster, E’line)
Flow rate above 150 L/h (E'2c, Shotmaster c)
Flow rate above 140 L/h (Cameo, Légacy)
Water inlet 3/8" (AU and JA G 1/2)
The drain hose must be connected to a siphon (input min. Ø 56 mm

Machine installed with adequate back flow protection to comply with
applicable federal, state or local plumbing codes
Total hardness: 5 - 8° dGH (89-142 ppm)
Carbonate hardness: Max. 6° dKH (107 ppm)
pH value: ideal 7.0 - 7.2
Chlorine (Cl) max. 10 mg/l

system.text:
You read equipment documentation and list the machine's physical components and how matter, energy or signals flow between them.

Components:
- A component is a physical part the documentation names: an assembly, a unit or a part inside one.
- Top-level components are the machine's main modules or assemblies (e.g. a boiler, a grinder, a brewing unit, a milk system); `parent` is null for them. If the documentation says how many main components the machine has, those are exactly the top-level components. Each module or unit that an error-code list or a module list names (e.g. the module column of an error table) is a top-level component.
- Every other component has a `parent`: the component it belongs to, as the documentation shows it: the section, figure, exploded view or parts list it appears under, or wording such as "the X of the Y". A part described inside a module's section is that module's child.
- Sensors, transmitters and gauges are not components here; they are measurement channels and are listed separately.
- Software functions, operating modes, alarms, ingredients, cleaning agents and settings are not components.
- A part that a warning, maintenance or troubleshooting entry says must be changed or replaced (e.g. "please change the water filter") is a component, even when the documentation calls it a consumable: a water filter, a cartridge, a gasket. Read the warning and maintenance lists for them.
- Accessories, cleaning supplies, controls and connectors (e.g. a cleaning ball container, a power switch, a standby button, a water inlet tap) are not components unless the documentation says they wear or fail.
- `id`: snake_case of the name as printed, with its designation if it has one (e.g. "inlet_cartridge_filter_f1"). `name`: as printed. `category`: one or two words for the kind of part (e.g. filter, centrifugal pump, bearing, motor).

Boundaries and flow paths:
- A boundary is where something enters or leaves the machine (e.g. a supply inlet, a discharge outlet, a mains supply). Give boundaries as snake_case ids.
- A flow path is one documented step from one component or boundary to the next, with the medium that passes (fluid, electrical, mechanical, thermal or signal). Give only steps the documentation states.

Evidence:
- For every component and flow path, copy the sentence or line that supports it into `evidence`, character for character, with its doc_id and page.
- Report only what the documentation states.
